item.title: AirLink 0.12.0-beta.2
item.description:
# AirLink 0.12.0 Beta 2
This beta focuses on transfers containing many small files, useful recovery advice and a diagnostic report you can save yourself.
## Changes
- Persist file checkpoints separately from the transfer header. A confirmed block commits its receipt, file offset and header together after the payload is synced. File completion no longer rewrites the complete folder manifest. - Avoid complete manifest copies in sender/receiver worker reads. Updated peers request compact per-file preparation and completion replies; old peers retain the legacy response. - Save a local diagnostic JSON from **Settings → About** on macOS, Linux and Windows. It contains version/platform information and aggregate counts, with no file/device names, private paths, addresses, identifiers, hashes, credentials, clipboard content or raw logs. No automatic upload. - Show understandable German/English recovery advice. Recognized recoverable sender failures offer **Try again**, retaining the original transfer, selected source identity and receiver checkpoints. Source changes, integrity failures, cancellation and terminal receiver failures require a new send. Technical errors remain under Details. - Keep the Arch native package as the straightforward installation option; document executable AppImage launching separately.
## Upgrade and installation
**The transfer database migrates on the first Beta 2 start.** Existing pairings, settings, confirmed progress and received files remain preserved. An interrupted migration rolls back. Beta 1 and older deliberately refuse an upgraded transfer database; downgrading that data directory is unsupported. Use a current beta on both computers to exercise the new compact peer path.
| System | Package | | --- | --- | | Apple Silicon, macOS 14+ | `macos-arm64.dmg` | | Intel, macOS 14+ | `macos-x64.dmg` | | Arch x64 | `linux-x64.pkg.tar.zst`; `sudo pacman -U ./AirLink-0.12.0-beta.2-linux-x64.pkg.tar.zst` | | Debian 12+ / Ubuntu 24.04+ x64 | `linux-x64.deb` | | Fedora / compatible openSUSE x64 | `linux-x64.rpm` | | Linux portable, x64 / glibc 2.36+ | `linux-x64.AppImage` | | Windows Intel/AMD | `windows-x64-setup.exe` | | Windows on ARM | `windows-arm64-setup.exe` |
All filenames begin with `AirLink-0.12.0-beta.2-`. The AppImage offers a user installation with application launcher. In Dolphin, enable **Properties → Permissions → Is executable** before launching; from a terminal use `chmod +x ./AirLink-0.12.0-beta.2-linux-x64.AppImage` followed by `./AirLink-0.12.0-beta.2-linux-x64.AppImage`. Do not open it as a shell script.
**Mac builds are ad hoc signed and not notarized.** First-open approval may be needed in System Settings → Privacy & Security. Replace only `/Applications/AirLink.app`, preserving separate app data and received files. Windows builds remain unsigned Setup installers. Automatic update notices require consent; download and installation require a click. Native Linux packages remain under package-manager control. From 0.11, install a matching 0.12 beta manually once to switch feeds.
## Measured performance
[Matched same-runner Linux TLS transfers](https://github.com/lucaskleinsteuber/Airlink/actions/runs/42774007494), including preparation and independent final structure/size/SHA-256 checks:
| Case | Beta 1 | Beta 2 | | --- | --- | --- | | 300 MiB single file, median of three each | 2.330 s | 1.895 s | | 4 GiB single file, median of three each | 28.973 s | 24.833 s | | 10,000 small files, Unicode and empty folders; one matched run each | 2,525.075 s | 79.541 s |
The 10,000-file result is about 32 times faster in this measured case. A separate three-run-per-version 1,000-file cohort improved from 18.869 to 4.919 seconds in the median. All measured candidate processes stayed below 76 MiB sampled RSS across the complete comparisons, restart tests and simultaneous transfers. These are Linux-runner loopback measurements, not Mac/Arch WLAN claims.
## Verification and limits
- [Windows, macOS and Ubuntu background suites passed](https://github.com/lucaskleinsteuber/Airlink/actions/runs/42774287811): Go race tests and vet, 74 Swift tests, 43 Windows Core tests with actual helper processes and 68 web tests/build. Windows x64 silent installation/upgrade/uninstall passed. ARM64 Windows is built and inspected, not executed. - [All six Linux package lifecycles passed](https://github.com/lucaskleinsteuber/Airlink/actions/runs/42774288049): Debian 12, Ubuntu 24.04, Arch, Fedora 45, openSUSE Leap 16 and Tumbleweed. Each ran 14 Qt Core tests, native/AppImage linkage and version checks, a genuine synthetic-next-version upgrade and data-preserving removal. Debian 12 / Qt 6.4 is the build baseline. - [Both Mac DMGs and Windows Setup architectures built](https://github.com/lucaskleinsteuber/Airlink/actions/runs/42774331052). Mac DMGs were additionally checked for version/build, architecture, ad hoc signature and the retained update key; all 74 Swift tests passed with the sealed ARM64 helper. The complete decoded package audit found no private-path/key/credential findings. - New regression cases cover atomic migration, 10,000-entry manifests without bulk checkpoint rewrites, failed commit/restart/replay, compact/legacy response compatibility, ownership, diagnostic redaction and a real two-service retry from a confirmed block.
The [verification record](https://github.com/lucaskleinsteuber/Airlink/blob/main/docs/TESTING.md) gives measurements and their scope. Application packages use source `7c4359b`; later documentation/feed changes preserve that application source. The signed manifest and SHA-256 checksums bind the eight packages to the existing update key. No desktop-controlling UI tests or application launches are used.
Physical Mac↔Arch WLAN throughput, native desktop rendering, Windows ARM64 runtime and the new 100-GB device test remain separate manual acceptance. Loopback measurements are not WLAN performance claims. This release remains a beta; full device and stability acceptance is required for 1.0.
